 BY ADV JOY JOSEPH (MANAYATHU), SC  THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 08.04.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 MACA. No.3751/2016  3  2025:KER:32667  JUDGMENT Dated this the 8th day of April, 2025
The petitioners in O.P.(M.V.) No.814/2010 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Perumbavoor are the appellants herein.

(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2.
The O.P. was filed under under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, by the parents and sisters of the deceased by name Manoj, who died in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 18.1.2010.

According to them, on 18.1.2010, at about 7 p.m. while the deceased was riding pillion on a motor cycle, a mini lorry bearing registration No. KL 7Y-7846 driven by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked him down and as a result of which he sustained serious injuries

Kannan vs Nassim on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19679498/
2 and he succumbed to the injuries, on the same day.
3. The 1st respondent is the driver, the 2nd respondent is the owner and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the mini lorry.
4th respondent is the insurer of the motor cycle.
According to the petitioners, the accident occurred due to 2025:KER:32667 the negligence of the driver of the mini lorry.
The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. was Rs.14,02,000/- limited to Rs.12,50,000/-.
4. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimonies of PW1 and PW2 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A14 and B1.
6.

After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.12,80,526/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioners preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

9. Heard Sri. Elson Simon, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioners/appellants, and Sri.
Joy Joseph Manayath, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioners is regarding the income of the deceased as fixed by the Tribunal.
As per the claim petition, the deceased was working as a painter, earning Rs.7,500/- per month, but the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.6000/-.The learned counsel for the insurer
would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.

11. The learned counsel relying upon the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Shivakumar M v.
Managing Director, BMTC [2017 KHC 6135]

entities.text:
Shivakumar M v.
Managing Director, BMTC [2017 KHC 6135]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , would argue that in the case of a painter involved in the accident of the year2013, the Apex Court has fixed the notional income at Rs.15,000/-.
As such the notional income of the deceased also is to be fixed in par with the above decision.
On a perusal of the above decision , it can be seen that in the above case the notional income claimed by the dependants of the deceased was 15,000/-.
In the instant case, the notional income claimed is only Rs.7500/-.
In the above circumstances, the above decision does not apply to the facts of this case.

3 12.

sentences.text: It is true that the petitioners could not prove the income of the 2025:KER:32667 deceased, as claimed in the OP.

As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, during the year 2010 will come to Rs.7500/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, considering the fact that the deceased was a painter by profession, his notional income is fixed at Rs.8500/-, for the purpose of computing the loss of dependency.
13. On the date of accident, the deceased was aged 25 years.

Therefore, 40% of the monthly income is liable to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 18, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121].

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the deceased was a bachelor who left behind 2 dependents, towards personal and living expense, 1/2 of the income is liable to be deducted, as held in Sarla Verma (supra).

In the above circumstances, the loss of dependency will come to Rs.12,85,200/-
14.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.25,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.3,00,000/- towards love 2025:KER:32667 and affection.
No compensation was awarded towards loss of consortium.

In the light of the decision in Pranay Sethi (supra), the appellants are entitled to get a consolidated sum of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.15,000/-
towards funeral expenses, and the dependents (parents, children and spouse) are entitled to get a sum of Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium, with an increase of 10% in every three years.

Therefore, towards loss of estate and funeral expense they are entitled to get a sum of Rs.18,150/-
each.

Towards loss of consortium, petitioners together are entitled to get a sum of Rs.96,800/-
(48,400 x 2).
15.

Since compensation for loss of consortium was given, further compensation for love and affection cannot be granted, in view of the decision in New India Assurance Company Ltd. v.
Somwati and Others, (2020) 9 SCC 644.

entities.text:
New India Assurance Company Ltd. v.
Somwati and Others, (2020) 9 SCC 644
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the compensation awarded towards love and affection is to be deducted.
16. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.5000/-, which according to the learned counsel for the petitioners, is on the lower side.
The deceased died in this case on the date of the accident.

In 2025:KER:32667 the above circumstances, I hold that the compensation awarded towards pain and suffering is on the lower side, and hence, it is enhanced to Rs.25,000/-.
17.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.

18. Therefore, the petitioners/appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.14,49,300/-,

The O.P. was filed under under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, by the parents and sisters of the deceased by name Manoj, who died in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 18.1.2010.
According to them, on 18.1.2010, at about 7 p.m. while the deceased was riding pillion on a motor cycle, a mini lorry bearing registration No. KL 7Y-7846 driven by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked him down and as a result of which he sustained serious injuries

opennyai_summary.issue:
8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?
opennyai_summary.arguments:
11. The learned counsel relying upon the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Shivakumar M v.
Managing Director, BMTC [2017 KHC 6135]
As such the notional income of the deceased also is to be fixed in par with the above decision.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is true that the petitioners could not prove the income of the 2025:KER:32667 deceased, as claimed in the OP.
As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, during the year 2010 will come to Rs.7500/-.
Therefore, considering the fact that the deceased was a painter by profession, his notional income is fixed at Rs.8500/-, for the purpose of computing the loss of dependency.
13. On the date of accident, the deceased was aged 25 years.
Therefore, 40% of the monthly income is liable to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 18, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121].
Since the deceased was a bachelor who left behind 2 dependents, towards personal and living expense, 1/2 of the income is liable to be deducted, as held in Sarla Verma (supra).
Since compensation for loss of consortium was given, further compensation for love and affection cannot be granted, in view of the decision in New India Assurance Company Ltd. v.
Somwati and Others, (2020) 9 SCC 644.
opennyai_summary.decision:
In the above circumstances, the loss of dependency will come to Rs.12,85,200/-
14.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.25,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.3,00,000/- towards love 2025:KER:32667 and affection.
In the light of the decision in Pranay Sethi (supra), the appellants are entitled to get a consolidated sum of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.15,000/-
towards funeral expenses, and the dependents (parents, children and spouse) are entitled to get a sum of Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium, with an increase of 10% in every three years.
Therefore, towards loss of estate and funeral expense they are entitled to get a sum of Rs.18,150/-
each.
Towards loss of consortium, petitioners together are entitled to get a sum of Rs.96,800/-
(48,400 x 2).
15.
Therefore, the compensation awarded towards love and affection is to be deducted.
16. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.5000/-, which according to the learned counsel for the petitioners, is on the lower side.
The deceased died in this case on the date of the accident.
In 2025:KER:32667 the above circumstances, I hold that the compensation awarded towards pain and suffering is on the lower side, and hence, it is enhanced to Rs.25,000/-.
17.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
18. Therefore, the petitioners/appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.14,49,300/-,
